payload.title: [native-android-2] callCommand / upsertObject deferreds never completed on disconnect or close — caller coroutin...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING native-android-2 (high/resource-leak, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/android/frick/src/main/java/dev/frick/client/FrickSyncSocket.kt
LINES: 453-457, 743-796, 826-840, 1086-1101

WHAT: pendingObjectWrites and pendingCallCommands map requestId -> CompletableDeferred and are ONLY drained when a matching Ack/Nack/CallCommandResult frame arrives (lines 860-919). On close() (826-840), onClosed (1086-1091) and onFailure (1093-1101) the maps are never iterated to fail outstanding deferreds — close() cancels the socket's own `scope`, but upsertObject()/callCommand() suspend on `deferred.await()` running on the CALLER's coroutine (FrickCallManager.issue at FrickCallManager.kt:513-522 awaits on the app/viewModel scope, not the socket scope). So a write/call frame sent just before a transport drop, server crash, or token expiry leaves its awaiter suspended indefinitely — the FrickCallManager join()/create()/leave() verb (and any upsertObject) never returns and never throws, hanging the UI flow that called it. Separately, there is no deferred.invokeOnCompletion cleanup: when the caller's coroutine is cancelled (e.g. viewModelScope teardown) the await() unwinds but the requestId entry stays in the ConcurrentHashMap for the socket's whole lifetime — an unbounded leak under churny screens/reconnects.

IMPACT: Permanent hang of call-control and object-write flows on any mid-flight disconnect (common on mobile), with no timeout and no error surfaced to the user. Plus a steady memory leak in pendingObjectWrites/pendingCallCommands as cancelled requests accumulate.

SUGGESTED FIX: On onClosed/onFailure/close(), drain both maps and complete every outstanding deferred with a Failed/exceptional result (e.g. a synthetic 'connection closed' envelope) so awaiters resume. Register deferred.invokeOnCompletion { pendingX.remove(requestId) } in upsertObject()/callCommand() to evict the entry on caller cancellation. Consider wrapping deferred.await() in withTimeout.
